Spice (spiciness at 0 dbar, TEOS-10) per CTD sample

Source: R/ctd_derived.R
ctd_spice.Rd

Rasmus Swalethorp's recipe (email 2026-09-22; CalCOFI/workflows#100), with the Gibbs SeaWater toolbox: absolute salinity from practical salinity, conservative temperature from in-situ temperature, then gsw_spiciness0() (McDougall & Krzysik 2015, J. Mar. Res. 73, 141-152). Positive is "spicy" (warm, salty), negative "minty" (cool, fresh). Pass the sensor-pair averaged, corrected series (temperature_ave, salinity_ave_corr), not a single sensor; a sample whose temperature or salinity is flagged 8/9 is NA.

Usage

ctd_spice(
  temperature,
  salinity,
  pressure,
  longitude,
  latitude,
  q_temperature = NA,
  q_salinity = NA
)

Arguments

temperature

in-situ temperature (deg C, ITS-90).

salinity

practical salinity (PSS-78).

pressure

sea pressure (dbar); depth in metres is an acceptable stand-in in the upper 500 m (the difference is < 1 %, well inside spice's sensitivity).

longitude, latitude

decimal degrees (recycled).

q_temperature, q_salinity

quality codes (NA = good).

Value

numeric vector, spiciness (kg m^-3).

Examples

ctd_spice(15, 33.5, 10, -120, 33)
#> [1] 1.173565
